message.content:
{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study quantitatively compares preclinical animal model results (tumor growth inhibition in mice) with human clinical outcomes (drug approval status) to assess predictive value, fitting the inclusion criteria for measuring agreement between animal results and human outcomes.",
  "arm": "efficacy",
  "arm_evidence": "The goal was to identify features of preclinical experiments or values of efficacy parameters that might predict a drug's success in clinical testing.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "oncology"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Preclinical Models of Lung Cancer Drugs.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "We conducted in-depth review of design and results of preclinical cell and murine model experiments used in the development of lung cancer drugs, quantitatively comparing 27 drugs that are now FDA approved for treatment of lung cancer with 167 drugs that failed to be approved for this purpose.",
  "species": [
    "mouse"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "For mouse model experiments was tumor growth inhibition (TGI) calculated as (tumor volume or weight of treated mice in mm 3 –tumor volume or weight of control mice in mm 3 )/tumor volume or weight of control mice in mm 3 at the end of the follow-up period.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The outcome variable for each analysis was drug approval status, scored as approved or failed. Independent variables included IC50 (cell studies) and TGI (animal studies)."
}
